relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: Kiyozō Kazama (風間 喜代三, Kazama Kiyozō; born 8 December 1928 in Tokyo) is a Japanese professor of comparative linguistics, specializing in Latin  and Greek, and emeritus professor at Tokyo University.

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: He studied comparative grammar under Kōzu Harushige at the department of linguistics at Tokyo University

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: He studied comparative grammar under Kōzu Harushige at the department of linguistics at Tokyo University, and graduated in 1952.

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: He studied abroad under a scholarship grant at Vienna University

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: returned to  become assistant, and then full, professor at his  alma mater.

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: He was awarded his doctorate in September 1978 on the subject of kinship terminology in Indo-European languages.

relations.subject: Kiyozō Kazama
relations.evidence: On his retirement, he subsequently taught at  Hosei University.
